expected: In the early nineteen hundreds, Coca-Cola faced scores of market copycats. Bottlers relied on plain cylinders, letting rivals mimic their scripted logos. Chilled paper labels also peeled away inside watery wooden ice tubs. So in nineteen fifteen, bottlers commissioned a completely unmistakable glass silhouette. Their brief demanded immediate recognition in total darkness or when shattered. Root Glass delivered distinctive ribs inspired by grooved cocoa pod sketches.
